commands.review_summary:
The PR resolves the spawned ACP session’s canonical store before persisting its label, avoids mutating a requester-side in-memory store for cross-agent spawns, and adds regression coverage for separate requester and target stores.

PR surface: Source +8, Tests +68. Total +76 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: a requester agent and spawned target agent use different store partitions, while current main writes the target session key through the requester path. This review did not run a live current-main Gateway reproduction.

target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `cursor` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:cursor:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `cursor`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:cursor:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/cursor/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via the existing `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` helper (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores are actually the same (same-agent spawn).

This is the narrowest fix — `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` is already used by three other ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`). No new infrastructure is needed.

The unmerged PR #57597 proposed this same approach; this implementation updates the naming and mock setup to match current `main` conventions (e.g. `updateSessionEntry` via Kysely, not `updateSessionStore`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cross-agent ACP spawn labels (`/acp spawn cursor --label novel`) were silently dropped. `/focus novel` failed. Only full session keys (`/focus agent:cursor:acp:<uuid>`) worked.
- **After**: Labels persist to the correct target store regardless of which agent issues the spawn. `/focus <label>` and `/acp status <label>` work as expected for cross-agent ACP sessions.
- Same-agent spawns are unaffected — the store path resolves to the same location and behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **67/67 passed** (includes pre-existing 66 tests + 1 new cross-agent regression test)
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts -t "cross-agent"` — new test `persists ACP spawn labels to the spawned session store (cross-agent, #106136)` passes, verifying `updateSessionEntry` is called with the **target** store path (`/tmp/codex-sessions.json`) and **not** the requester path (`/tmp/requester-sessions.json`)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp/lifecycle.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **clean**
- `pnpm format` — **clean** on changed files
- Autoreview: **PASSED** — no P0/P1 findings; best-fix judgment confirmed (`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` is the canonical helper used by sibling ACP metadata operations)

Behavior addressed: ACP spawn label cross-agent store-partition mismatch
Real environment tested: Vitest (colocated unit tests with mocked `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp`)
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: 67 tests passed; new cross-agent test verifies label is written to target store at `/tmp/codex-sessions.json` while requester store at `/tmp/requester-sessions.json` is untouched
Observed result after fix: Label persists to the correct target agent's session store; request store is not mutated for cross-agent spawns
What was not tested: End-to-end cross-agent ACP spawn with real Gateway + Feishu + Cursor harness due to credential/backend requirements. The bug is reproduced from code-level analysis verified by the reported persistence state and the focused unit-test coverage of both same-agent and cross-agent store resolution paths.
